Learning Theory: Trustworthy AI Foundations

What makes learning reliable under adversarial data, supervision, and evaluation?

Core algorithms and theory for trustworthy machine learning, from adversarial training and robust generalisation to representation alignment.

Research focus

Three questions shape this programme.

This is the working agenda: a precise statement of the problems the lab is building toward, not a claim that every component is already solved.

01

Robust generalisation

Understand when robustness transfers beyond the training sample—and why accuracy and robustness sometimes compete.

02

Reliable representations

Study how contrastive and foundation-model representations become aligned, stable, and diagnostically useful.

03

Principled intervention

Turn theoretical failure analysis into training objectives, sample-selection rules, and measurable guarantees.
